markdown_report:
The best first experiment remains a **prefix-aligned BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter**, revised to separate contract correctness, training-exposed recovery and behavioral sensitivity. At 0% progress, reliable measurements should precede architectural changes. No measured results were supplied.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training-position margins cannot establish appended-mask generalization. Prefix probes on training events remain in-sample. (2) Qualitative feedback motivates testing recent-history dependence, but cannot establish ownership or current needs. (3) Empty samples need counts and unavailable results; zeros can falsely suggest healthy behavior.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) motivates masked supervision and appended-mask prediction. [BERT masking](https://github.com/google-research/bert/blob/master/create_pretraining_data.py) permits unchanged selected tokens, so provenance checks must follow corruption branches. (2) [Robust Training](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) motivates history interventions, but compacted deletions also change positions. Transfer to BERT4Rec requires measurement. (3) [Interpreting User Inaction](https://will-qianzhao.github.io/pubs/zhao2018recsys-a.pdf) distinguishes nonselection reasons. Deferred and unidentified items must not become rejection labels.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Evidence | Gap addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Contract integrity | Provenance, attention, readout, reload fixtures | Invalid diagnostic scores |
| Behavioral sensitivity | Paired removals and position-preserving controls | Content/position confounding |
| Feedback interpretation | Explicit statements and available text | Rejection versus uncertainty |

**Candidate algorithms.** Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-aligned contract adapter [BERT4Rec] | 4/7/5 | Originality: useful integration; established components. Potential: enables reliable evolution; no direct ranking improvement. Difficulty: reuses ModelView; independent fixtures and provenance require integration. |
| Paired recency sensitivity probe [Robust Training] | 5/7/6 | Originality: controlled BERT4Rec adaptation; interventions already exist. Potential: guides masking experiments; sensitivity need not imply preference quality. Difficulty: shared scoring; position controls require attention hooks. |
| Evidence-coded feedback audit [User Inaction] | 4/6/3 | Originality: connects uncertainty to diagnosis; established taxonomy. Potential: prevents false labels; sparse feedback. Difficulty: simple schema; manual adjudication remains. |

**Selected algorithm.** Preserve the corrected BERT4Rec and gate interpretation on provenance, padding, bidirectionality and fresh-process predictor-parity checks. Use independent short, full-length, empty and repeated-ID fixtures, plus deliberately shifted labels, omitted masks and incorrect readout as structural positive controls. Unchanged corruption branches and legitimate repeated IDs must pass.

Construct training-only prefixes by withholding a target event and later context, reserving one slot for the appended mask. Report these as training-exposed recovery, stratified by target repetition; withholding input does not undo parameter exposure. Host validation remains the generalization evidence.

Freeze checkpoints and candidates. Compare equal-sized recent/older compacted removals with in-place masking and position-preserving attention deletion; none represents neutral absence. Report paired rank, margin, HR@10 and overlap changes, counts and user-bootstrap intervals. These measure model sensitivity, not causal preferences. Preserve adapter interfaces, report unavailable quantities explicitly, leave category-metadata breakdowns empty, and select exclusively using unchanged macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Implement a prefix-aligned diagnostic adapter that verifies BERT4Rec training/inference integrity before measuring history sensitivity, explicitly separating training-exposed recovery from held-out generalization. Retain exactly one independently trained BERT4Rec model per category.
idea.motivation: Training-position margins can obscure deployment mismatch, and empty samples can appear healthy. Qualitative feedback motivates investigating recent-history dependence but provides no numerical evidence that recency interventions improve HR@10. Training-event recovery can reflect memorization, while compacted history deletion confounds removed content with changed positional embeddings.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model as the actual trained nn.Module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. Preserve the loader's (None, sequence, positive, negative) tuple with B x L tensors. Add optional sampler instrumentation recording original tokens, selected positions, corruption branches, corrupted inputs and loss weights. Assert selected labels equal original tokens at the same positions and unselected/padding positions contribute no loss. Validate MASK/random/unchanged branches separately under the baseline's actual policy; unchanged tokens and random replacements matching originals are permitted when that policy allows them. Detect shifted-label exposure using event/position provenance, never repeated item identity alone. Report provenance unavailable when instrumentation is absent. Inspect effective attention masks; use a controlled nondegenerate attention fixture to verify influence from a valid token right of an interior query. Perturb padding embeddings while holding positions and masks fixed and require unchanged valid outputs; perturb an allowed token as a positive control. Exclude padding from attention keys, targets and loss. Independently construct empty, short, full-length and repeated-ID inference fixtures; truncate history to L-1, append the reserved mask, left-pad and read the appended mask's absolute index, never nonpadding count minus one. Full-length fixtures must reserve mask space. Reload each category's single checkpoint through the generated predictor in a fresh process, verifying configuration, item mapping, preprocessing, exact IDs/masks, finite candidate scores and ordering. Compare live/reloaded float32 scores in eval and inference modes with initial rtol=1.3e-6 and atol=1e-5; record maximum errors and inspect near ties instead of silently widening tolerances. Construct diagnostic prefixes exclusively from training histories, excluding the withheld target occurrence and all later events while retaining legitimate earlier occurrences of its item. Label results training-exposed recovery; they do not measure held-out generalization or prove memorization alone. Stratify by whether the target item appears in the prefix. Use existing host validation solely under its fixed protocol; do not introduce new splits. For auxiliary candidates, include the positive exactly once and sample unique negatives excluding it, padding, mask and all items in that user's permitted training history. Record this policy and actual candidate counts; if fewer than 99 negatives are available, retain all eligible negatives and report the smaller count. Do not modify host candidates. Reuse each original candidate set across interventions without recomputing exclusions. Freeze one checkpoint/category, disable dropout and predefine paired blocks: for a retained history of n>=2 items, choose k=min(3,floor(n/2)); remove its oldest k or newest k items. Compare compacted deletion with in-place mask replacement retaining original positions/visibility and attention deletion blocking removed slots as keys/values while preserving survivor positions and the final inference mask. Use diagnostic-only optional hooks without changing existing ModelView call signatures; mark attention deletion unavailable if unsupported. Mask replacement introduces learned content, attention deletion changes normalization, and compaction changes positions; none is neutral absence. Record paired target score/rank, margins, HR@10 and top-10 overlap, defined as intersection size divided by the smaller returned list length. Summarize per category, training-popularity quartile and history-length quartile, recording cutpoints and counts. Use up to 200 eligible users/category selected with seed 42 and one last eligible training event/user; use all available eligible users if fewer. Use 1,000 seeded user-bootstrap resamples with all prefixes/interventions for a user grouped together; report percentile 95% intervals and equal-category macro-averages only when all four categories have eligible observations. Repeat auxiliary candidate draws with predefined seeds 42, 43 and 44 and report each draw separately; this changes no training seed or host evaluation seed. Exclude padding and mask embeddings from the existing collapse probe and retain its seed-42 sampling of up to 2,048 embeddings, cosine definition and limitations. Retain existing training-margin metrics with explicit sample counts and exposure labels. Return null plus a reason when no eligible observations exist; never substitute healthy zeros. Keep unavailable category-metadata breakdowns empty. Evidence-code qualitative feedback as explicit rejection, deferred interest, positive interest or unresolved identification with excerpts and counts; never infer unavailable ownership, mood, compatibility or preference labels from missing metadata. Preserve four-category routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Any architecture change must also update the embedded predictor writer. No ensembles, checkpoint averaging, external data or pretrained weights are introduced. Structural fixtures require no retraining, but all host execution remains within the shared search budget. The baseline source was not supplied, so these are reproducible integration requirements rather than a verified implementation.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
  def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save model mode; set evaluation mode
    initialize metrics, definitions, counts, unavailable_reasons
    under inference_mode():
      run independent token, padding, bidirectional-attention and readout fixtures
      inspect optional sampler provenance:
        assert selected labels equal original tokens at their positions
        assert unselected and padding positions have zero loss weight
        validate each actual corruption branch, allowing unchanged targets
      require shifted-label, omitted-mask and wrong-readout controls to fail
      compare live and fresh-process generated-predictor scores:
        require identical configuration, item mapping, IDs and masks
        require finite scores and allclose(rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5)
        record maximum errors and investigate ordering differences
      retain existing collapse and training-margin probes with sample counts
      select up to 200 eligible training users/category with seed 42
      for each selected user:
        choose last eligible training target event
        prefix = events strictly before that event, truncated to L-1
        retain legitimate earlier occurrences of the target item
        input = left_pad(prefix + [MASK], L)
        readout = absolute position of appended MASK
        mark target event as training-exposed; record repeat/explore stratum
        for candidate_seed in [42, 43, 44]:
          candidates = positive once + up to 99 unique eligible negatives
          freeze candidates and original-history exclusion rules
          record original target score, rank, margins and HR@10
          k = min(3, floor(len(prefix)/2))
          for block in [oldest_k, newest_k]:
            for intervention in [compact_delete, in_place_MASK, attention_delete]:
              preserve final inference mask; preserve slots for last two modes
              if intervention unsupported: record unavailable reason
              else: score identical candidates and record paired changes
          record recent-minus-older paired contrasts per intervention
      aggregate per category and recorded history/popularity quartiles
      report candidate draws separately and user-bootstrap 95% intervals
      compute equal-category macro summaries only with all categories eligible
      return null plus reason for empty metrics; retain empty metadata breakdowns
    restore model mode in finally block
    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
  embed measured metrics, definitions, counts, exposure labels,
    uncertainty, candidate policy and unavailable reasons
  request JSON with status, core_findings, key_implications and evidence
  distinguish structural failures, training-exposed sensitivity,
    qualitative hypotheses and unchanged host validation
  prohibit causal preference claims or generalization claims from training recovery

originality.positive: Combines family-specific provenance, independent predictor checks and controlled behavioral probes within the existing diagnostic interface.
originality.negative: The checks and interventions are established techniques; their integration does not constitute a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: Can provide trustworthy evidence for subsequent single-model masking and architecture experiments while distinguishing positional effects and missing evidence.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostics alone cannot establish improved validation HR@10, and training-exposed probes can reward memorization or popularity shortcuts.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing ModelView scoring and probe aggregation remain reusable, and small structural fixtures require no retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Sampler provenance, independent fresh-process reload checks and position-preserving attention interventions require careful integration with the unavailable baseline source.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides masked-item bidirectional recommendation and appended-mask prediction.
Its learned absolute positional embeddings motivate separating content removal from positional reindexing.
limitations: Does not establish correctness of the host sampler, padding, checkpoint writer or diagnostic implementation.
Withholding a training event from diagnostic input does not remove its prior parameter-training exposure.

related_work.title: BERT pretraining data creation implementation
contributions: Documents selected-position provenance and MASK/random/unchanged corruption branches.
limitations: The host's actual corruption policy must be inspected; BERT's policy must not be assumed mandatory for every BERT4Rec implementation.

related_work.title: RecTools transformer tutorial
contributions: Documents padding-only attention and appended-mask inference conventions.
limitations: Library conventions do not verify the host implementation or substitute for independent fixtures.

related_work.title: PyTorch testing documentation
contributions: Provides explicit float32 comparison tolerances for initial predictor-parity checks.
limitations: Numerical closeness does not guarantee identical ordering for near-tied candidates or correct preprocessing.

related_work.title: Robust Training (2024; supplied search result)
contributions: Motivates measuring ranking sensitivity to recent-interaction removal and ranking overlap.
limitations: The supplied summary concerns GRU/SASRec variants; BERT4Rec transfer requires measurement.
Sensitivity does not establish causal changes in user preferences.

related_work.title: Xu et al. (2021; supplied history-replacement reference)
contributions: Motivates preserving history length during replacement interventions.
limitations: The proposed mask and attention-deletion controls are adaptations, not an established BERT4Rec causal-identification protocol.
Replacement, deletion and masking each introduce distinct perturbations.

related_work.title: RepeatNet: A Repeat Aware Neural Recommendation Machine for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Distinguishes repeat targets from exploration targets, motivating repetition strata and preservation of legitimate earlier target-item occurrences.
limitations: Repeat-item prediction does not distinguish generalization from training-event recovery without exposure labels.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Auxiliary candidate diagnostics therefore remain specific to their declared sampling protocol and cannot replace the pinned host metric.

related_work.title: Interpreting User Inaction
contributions: Motivates distinguishing deferred interest and other reasons for nonselection from explicit rejection.
limitations: Provides no preference labels for these four Amazon datasets and does not justify inferring unobserved ownership, mood or intent.
